evidence: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis (Figure 2b) confirmed the preparation of fluorite-type cubic CeO2 (a ¼ 0.540 nm, JCPDS: 810792). Micro-Raman analysis (Figure 2c) confirmed that inverse opal powders were made of nanocrystalline cubic ceria, with no evidence of either tetragonal distortion of the oxygen lattice or residual organic impurities due to the template removal step. XRR measurements on TiO2 thin films deposited under the same conditions on natively oxidized Si(100) single-crystal substrates were carried out. Glancing-angle X-ray diffraction (GAXRD) was performed on CeO2 inverse opals after coating for 300, 450, and 600 ALD cycles. 2D XRD (XRD 2) analyses were carried out on inverse opals coated with the thinnest (about 10 nm thick) TiO2 layers. SEM images were acquired. UV/Vis spectroscopy showed that the CeO2/TiO2 core–shell inverse opals are active toward MB degradation. Optical reflectivity and SEM images showed that the colloidal spheres crystallize in the face-centered cubic (fcc) system.
